title: Fit native stellar-system overview to the active viewport with the existing camera authority

scope.subject: Reuse the existing YEIS native-system adapter and camera-controls fit-sphere path so the 7.0-unit overview remains fully framed on portrait and narrow viewports without shrinking the system or adding device-specific shots

research_summary: Hosted tablet/mobile System screenshots added after the floating-origin fix show the native system itself is now correctly scaled, but the fixed System camera distance is not viewport-aware: the 390x844 case clips the outer orbit through both horizontal edges because PerspectiveCamera horizontal FOV narrows with aspect ratio. Personal Universe already uses camera-controls getDistanceToFitSphere() for Approach/Orbit framing. Reuse that same camera authority for System: expose the existing 7.0 native overview radius as one shared product/render budget, preserve the current System view direction and transition semantics, and derive only the camera distance from the active camera aspect/FOV. Do not shrink YEIS geometry, add mobile shot tables, or mount another camera.

sources.finding: The already-installed camera-controls implementation provides getDistanceToFitSphere(), which derives the required distance from the active perspective camera FOV/aspect and therefore matches the existing close-world framing authority.
React Three Fiber exposes one active Three.js camera/viewport lifecycle; the existing CinematicCamera can react to that camera projection without a second mobile camera or renderer.
A perspective camera's visible horizontal extent depends on aspect ratio, so a fixed world-space distance that looks correct at 1440x900 can crop the same bounded system on a portrait viewport.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the pinned YEIS native-system renderer and the corrected floating-origin adapter as the full system authority; the geometry should not be replaced or rescaled per device.
Keep the single R3F PerspectiveCamera and viewport lifecycle; the framing correction belongs in the existing camera host rather than a parallel mobile render path.
camera-controls already owns cinematic transitions and viewport-aware fit-distance calculation, covering the framing gap directly.
Reuse getDistanceToFitSphere() with the existing System shot direction and shared overview radius; no new camera component is required.

candidates.name: Existing pinned-YEIS native system plus product adapter
candidates.source: Current YeisSystemScene native renderer and floating-origin adapter
candidates.reason: The hosted evidence confirms the native system geometry and restored floating-origin coordinates are correct; only camera framing changes with viewport aspect.

candidates.name: Existing camera-controls fit-sphere distance for System
candidates.reason: It already solves the same aspect/FOV-aware framing problem for product worlds while preserving the existing camera transition and settlement authority.

candidates.name: Separate desktop/tablet/mobile System camera tables
candidates.source: New project-owned viewport breakpoints and shot constants
candidates.reason: Would duplicate framing policy, create breakpoint drift, and solve a projection-math problem less robustly than the existing camera-controls fit calculation.

candidates.name: Viewport-specific native-system geometry shrink
candidates.source: New adapter scale branch by viewport
candidates.reason: Would undo the corrected native overview scale, alter click/focus geometry presentation by device, and mix camera composition concerns into the renderer adapter.

decision.rationale: Keep the corrected YEIS native-system geometry unchanged and reuse the existing camera-controls fit-sphere computation to derive System camera distance from the active viewport. Share the existing 7.0 overview radius between renderer and camera, retain the current System direction/target/transition semantics, and validate desktop/tablet/mobile System screenshots with the already-running Playwright visual suite.
decision.fallback: If a sphere fit proves visually too conservative, adjust only the shared framing breathing-room factor while retaining the same camera-controls authority; do not add device-specific shots or rescale native system geometry.
